oidc_jwt.description: Successful JWT/OIDC login creates or uses an identity entity alias whose name is taken from the configured user_claim value, not necessarily the JWT sub claim.
oidc_jwt.source: JWT/OIDC role docs: user_claim is used as the name for the Identity entity alias created due to successful login.
oidc_jwt.note: I4 comparisons must use the configured identity claim as the expected alias source when it differs from sub.

oidc_jwt.description: Token self-lookup display_name includes auth mount metadata as a prefix before the upstream identity value.
oidc_jwt.source: Token lookup-self example shows display_name like ldap2-tesla; auth path is included in token display names.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag mount-path prefixes as identity-collision bugs when the suffix matches the sent identity value.

oidc_jwt.description: JWT bearer replay is not documented as prevented by jti tracking in the JWT auth method; repeated use of the same valid JWT may succeed by design until the JWT expires.
oidc_jwt.source: Vault JWT auth docs describe signature and claim validation but no jti replay cache; RFC 7519 makes jti optional.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not report replay_same_token on plain JWT login as a vulnerability absent stronger freshness guarantees such as one-time assertions.

oidc_jwt.description: Vault JWT auth does not document jti tracking or one-time JWT consumption; replaying the same valid JWT can succeed multiple times and yield multiple Vault tokens.
oidc_jwt.source: Vault JWT auth API docs only describe signature/claim validation and token issuance, with no jti replay cache.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not report replay_same_token or stateless_jwt_no_jti as a vulnerability for JWT auth; treat as stateless verifier behavior unless a separate one-time mechanism is configured.

oidc_jwt.description: Vault identity OIDC provider clients deny all entities by default unless assignments are configured; allow_all must be set to permit all entities.
oidc_jwt.source: OIDC provider client docs: by default, no Vault entities are allowed; allow_all permits all.
oidc_jwt.note: Authorization failures from unassigned clients are expected setup behavior, not evidence of broken login or scope enforcement.

oidc_jwt.description: An OIDC provider with empty allowed_client_ids allows no clients, while '*' allows all clients.
oidc_jwt.source: OIDC provider API docs for allowed_client_ids.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not interpret an empty list as wildcard access.

oidc_jwt.description: When group_policy_application_mode is set to 'any', identity group policies apply across namespace boundaries by design.
oidc_jwt.note: Cross-namespace policy reach in this mode is configured behavior, not an authorization-binding flaw.

oidc_jwt.description: Vault OIDC provider requires PKCE for public clients in the authorization code flow.
oidc_jwt.source: OIDC provider client docs: public clients must use PKCE; token endpoint docs require code_verifier for public clients.
oidc_jwt.note: A rejected code exchange without code_verifier for a public client is expected behavior, not a bug.

oidc_jwt.constraint: Exactly one of oidc_discovery_url, jwks_url, and jwt_validation_pubkeys must be set in configure_jwt_validation. jwks_pairs is an alternate JWKS source and cannot be combined with jwks_url/jwks_ca_pem; bound_issuer cannot be configured when jwks_pairs is set. Misconfiguring these trust-anchor inputs makes I1 signature and issuer tests invalid.

When testing I1 issuer validation or trust_anchor_substitution, configure_jwt_validation MUST include bound_issuer unless the test intentionally exercises the jwks_pairs exception. If bound_issuer is omitted, Vault will not compare the JWT iss claim, so issuer-mismatch tests can pass trivially for the wrong reason.

Every JWT/OIDC role must have at least one bound value configured. The role API states at least one bound value must be set; otherwise setup is invalid. For JWT roles with an aud claim (typical case), bound_audiences is required and the JWT aud must match at least one configured audience.

bound_subject supports exact string match only; there is no companion type parameter. For I4 multi-identity tests, OMIT bound_subject entirely rather than setting wildcards. Setting bound_subject to '*' matches only the literal subject '*'.

bound_audiences is exact membership matching against JWT aud values; there is no wildcard/glob mode. For I4 scenarios requiring multiple different audiences to pass the same role, do not use a wildcard placeholder in bound_audiences; either omit audience binding where the test allows it or configure explicit acceptable audience values.

bound_claims matching semantics are controlled by bound_claims_type. Default bound_claims_type='string' means values are treated as literals and must match exactly; '*' is literal, not wildcard. For I4 multi-identity tests that need multiple different claim values to pass, either omit the exact-match claim constraint or explicitly set bound_claims_type='glob' and use glob patterns.

For I5 numeric coercion tests on bound_claims, set bound_claims_type to 'glob' rather than the default 'string'. The docs state bound_claims values may be string, integer, boolean, or list, but default string mode treats values as exact literals; using glob mode is required so non-string JWT claim values are coerced to strings instead of being rejected outright.

user_claim must resolve to a string claim value. If user_claim_json_pointer is false, user_claim is interpreted literally as a claim name; if true, it uses JSON Pointer syntax. Misconfiguring this changes which upstream identity value becomes the alias name and can invalidate I4 principal-binding tests.

groups_claim must resolve to a list of strings. Sending a scalar string where a list is required can cause login failure unrelated to the intended I4/I5 test. For type-confusion tests, distinguish platform rejection of wrong type from identity-collision behavior.
clock_skew_leeway has sentinel semantics for JWT roles: value 0 means use the default 60 seconds of leeway, while value -1 disables extra leeway. Never assume 0 means strict zero-skew validation.

expiration_leeway has sentinel semantics for JWT roles: value 0 means use the default 150 seconds of leeway, while value -1 disables extra leeway. Never assume 0 means immediate expiration enforcement.
not_before_leeway has sentinel semantics for JWT roles: value 0 means use the default 150 seconds of leeway, while value -1 disables extra leeway. Never assume 0 means strict nbf enforcement.

For I2 expired_token and future_token tests, include a CONTROL login using a valid JWT alongside the attack JWT. Also set exp/nbf relative to Vault's leeway behavior using {{now_epoch}}, {{now_epoch_plus_N}}, and {{now_epoch_minus_N}}; otherwise a rejection may be caused by setup or default leeway rather than the intended freshness check.

token_num_uses limits every API call made with the issued Vault session token, including verify_granted_identity and verify_read_secret. If the sequence performs both self-lookup and a protected read, the minimum safe token_num_uses is 2; use 3+ if additional session-authenticated verification calls are present.

For I3 config-change tests, Vault applies updated auth mount config and role config to NEW logins by design. A valid coherence test must compare repeated authentications of the same upstream proof before and after the admin change, not treat the mere existence of changed behavior after reconfiguration as a bug.

For I3 jwt_default_role_change tests, login_with_jwt may omit role and then uses the mount's default_role. To test default-role coherence, the login request MUST omit role entirely; supplying role explicitly bypasses the default-role behavior under test.

For OIDC-flow tests against Vault's JWT/OIDC auth method, the code exchange operation is Vault's callback endpoint /v1/auth/{mount}/oidc/callback, not the upstream provider token endpoint. Using the provider token endpoint tests the wrong system and invalidates I3 flow-coherence results.

OIDC redirect URIs must exactly match configured allowed_redirect_uris on the role, and for Vault's identity OIDC provider clients, redirect_uri must exactly match one of the client's redirect_uris. Redirect mismatch failures are expected setup errors, not security findings.

Public OIDC clients on Vault's identity OIDC provider must use PKCE for the authorization code flow; confidential clients may use PKCE optionally. For pkce_skip and pkce_not_required_public_client checks, assert non-200/error outcomes directly rather than comparing identities.

Vault identity OIDC provider clients default to allowing no entities unless assignments are configured; to allow all entities, the client must include the built-in allow_all assignment. If using Vault as the upstream OIDC provider in JWT/OIDC flow tests, missing assignments will cause authorization failures unrelated to the invariant under test.

Vault identity OIDC provider allowed_client_ids has special semantics: empty means no clients are allowed, while '*' means all clients are allowed. Do not treat empty as wildcard during provider setup.
KV v2 verify_read_secret must use the /data/ path segment. Using /v1/{engine}/{path} hits KV v1 semantics and returns 404/permission errors for the wrong reason.

To list KV v2 secrets, Vault requires list capability on the /metadata/ path even if reads and writes use /data/. If a test seeds or verifies resources via listing, policy setup must grant metadata list separately or failures will be false positives.

External identity groups should be used with group aliases for external auth-derived membership. For JWT groups_claim mapping tests, create an identity group and bind the external group name via create_group_alias rather than trying to model external membership with manual member_entity_ids.

Group policy application can be globally configured via /sys/config/group-policy-application. In Enterprise, mode 'within_namespace_hierarchy' versus 'any' changes whether group policies apply across namespace boundaries. I5 group-policy escalation tests must account for this global mode to avoid misclassifying by-design cross-namespace policy application.
configure_jwt_validation MUST set exactly one of oidc_discovery_url, jwks_url, or jwt_validation_pubkeys. Vault rejects or misconfigures validation if more than one or none are set.
configure_jwt_validation MUST NOT combine bound_issuer with jwks_pairs. Vault documentation states bound_issuer cannot be configured when jwks_pairs is set.

create_auth_role requires at least one bound value to be set. For JWT roles, the fuzzer MUST configure at least one of bound_audiences, bound_subject, or bound_claims; otherwise role creation/setup is invalid.

For JWT roles that contain an aud claim (typical case), bound_audiences is required and the JWT aud MUST match at least one configured audience. I5 audience tests must explicitly configure bound_audiences; omitting it can make the test invalid or role creation semantically incomplete.

bound_subject supports EXACT string match only. There is no companion bound_subject_type parameter. Wildcards like '*' are treated literally, not as patterns. For I4 multi-identity tests, OMIT bound_subject entirely rather than setting a wildcard.

user_claim is used as the identity alias name and the claim value MUST be a string. I4 tests that vary claim types must keep user_claim on a string-valued claim or login will fail for type reasons rather than identity-binding reasons.
groups_claim value MUST be a list of strings. For I4 type-confusion group tests, a scalar string groups claim is expected to fail type validation rather than map equivalently to a one-element list.

bound_claims_type defaults to 'string', where bound_claims values are treated as literals and must match exactly. For I4 multi-identity scenarios, exact-match bound_claims entries MUST be omitted if multiple distinct values need to pass; do NOT set '*' unless bound_claims_type is explicitly set to 'glob'.
For I5 wildcard tests on bound_claims, the fuzzer MUST set bound_claims_type='glob'. If left at the default 'string', '*' is a literal asterisk and will not match arbitrary claim values.

bound_claims accepts expected values as string, integer, boolean, or list of strings. Because the default bound_claims_type='string' treats values as literals and exact matches, for I5 numeric coercion tests the fuzzer SHOULD set bound_claims_type='glob' so numeric claim values are coerced to strings rather than being rejected outright by strict literal handling.
clock_skew_leeway has sentinel semantics: value 0 means use the default 60 seconds, not literal zero; value -1 disables the extra leeway. Never assume 0 means strict checking.
expiration_leeway has sentinel semantics: value 0 means use the default 150 seconds, not literal zero; value -1 disables the extra leeway. Never assume 0 means strict expiration enforcement.
not_before_leeway has sentinel semantics: value 0 means use the default 150 seconds, not literal zero; value -1 disables the extra leeway. Never assume 0 means strict nbf enforcement.

For I2 expired_token and future_token tests, the fuzzer MUST override leeway settings away from their defaults if it needs strict boundary behavior. Using 0 does NOT mean zero leeway on Vault JWT roles; use -1 to disable extra leeway or a small explicit duration.

For I2 token-freshness tests (expired_token, future_token, nbf), the sequence MUST include a CONTROL login using a valid token alongside the ATTACK login. Without a control, a failed JWT login cannot be distinguished from broken Vault JWT configuration.

For I1 issuer-validation tests, configure_jwt_validation MUST include bound_issuer. If bound_issuer is omitted, Vault will not compare the JWT iss claim against a configured issuer and issuer-mismatch tests become meaningless.

For I1 signing-key rotation and trust-anchor substitution tests, the fuzzer MUST configure trust using exactly one source and then mutate that same source. Mixing oidc_discovery_url, jwks_url, and jwt_validation_pubkeys in setup is invalid on Vault and will confound trust-anchor tests.

For I3 jwt_signing_key_rotation tests, after changing jwks_url or jwt_validation_pubkeys, the fuzzer must perform a NEW login attempt. Existing Vault tokens are independent sessions; the coherence test is about re-authentication under updated trust, not retroactive invalidation of already-issued Vault tokens.
For I3 jwt_default_role_change tests, login_with_jwt MUST omit the role parameter so Vault uses default_role. Supplying an explicit role bypasses the default-role behavior and invalidates the test.

For I3 OIDC callback tests, allowed_redirect_uris on the role and redirect_uri used in the OIDC flow must exactly match one configured value. Redirect mismatch failures are by design and should be asserted via HTTP status, not treated as identity-binding issues.

OIDC public clients in Vault MUST use PKCE for the authorization code flow, and code_verifier is required at the token endpoint for public clients. Tests that omit code_verifier against a public client should expect flow rejection by status code.

OIDC confidential clients may use PKCE but are not required to. For pkce_skip hardening checks, interpret behavior in the context of client_type: omission of code_verifier is only inherently invalid for public clients or codes granted with PKCE.

OIDC client redirect_uris must exactly match the redirect_uri used in authorization requests, and the token endpoint redirect_uri must match the one used when the code was generated. I3 redirect_uri mismatch tests should assert rejection via status code only.

OIDC provider clients default to allowing no entities unless assignments are configured; to allow all entities, the built-in assignment 'allow_all' must be supplied. Any Vault-as-IdP OIDC test using identity/oidc/provider endpoints must configure assignments explicitly or authentication may fail by design.

OIDC provider allowed_client_ids has special semantics: empty means no clients are allowed, while '*' means all clients are allowed. Do not treat empty and wildcard as equivalent in authorization-binding tests.

Identity group aliases for external groups require the auth mount accessor and a canonical internal group ID. For JWT groups_claim policy tests, the fuzzer MUST create an external identity group and then create a group alias bound to the JWT auth mount accessor; manually setting member_entity_ids on an external group is not the correct binding mechanism.

External identity groups are intended to be populated through aliases from auth methods. For JWT group-policy tests, use create_group_alias with the JWT mount accessor rather than trying to model upstream groups via direct entity membership edits.

KV v2 metadata listing uses /metadata/ paths and requires list capability there even if reads/writes use /data/. If the fuzzer seeds or inspects KV v2 paths beyond direct reads, policies must include the correct /metadata/ capabilities.
KV v2 engine config max_versions has sentinel semantics: value 0 means keep the default 10 versions, not zero versions. Do not interpret 0 as disabling version retention.
KV v2 delete_version_after has sentinel semantics: value '0s' means do not schedule automatic deletion. This is a special disable sentinel, not an instruction to delete immediately.

For I5 group_policy_escalation tests in Enterprise, /sys/config/group-policy-application changes whether group policies apply only within namespace hierarchy or from any namespace. Cross-namespace policy inheritance may therefore be by design when mode='any'.

For I1 issuer-validation tests, configure_jwt_validation MUST include bound_issuer unless the test intentionally exercises the no-issuer-binding case. If bound_issuer is omitted, Vault does not compare the JWT iss claim.
bound_issuer cannot be configured when jwks_pairs is set. Do not use jwks_pairs for issuer-enforcement tests that require bound_issuer.

create_auth_role requires at least one bound value to be set. A valid setup must include at least one of bound_audiences, bound_subject, or bound_claims (or other documented bound values) or role creation is invalid.

For JWT roles carrying an aud claim, bound_audiences is required and the JWT aud must match at least one configured audience. Do not interpret rejection of a token with aud and no bound_audiences as a vulnerability; it is required configuration.

user_claim is required and its claim value must be a string. I4 tests that vary identity type must keep the selected user_claim string-typed or Vault will reject the login before identity binding is exercised.

groups_claim must resolve to a list of strings. For I4/I5 group-mapping tests, a JWT groups claim sent as a bare string instead of a string array is expected to fail type validation rather than map equivalently.

bound_subject supports EXACT string match only; there is no companion type parameter. Wildcards like '*' are treated literally. For I4 multi-identity tests, OMIT bound_subject entirely rather than setting a wildcard.

bound_audiences performs membership matching against JWT aud values; there is no wildcard/glob mode parameter. For multi-identity scenarios that need varying audiences to pass, do not set a wildcard audience string; either configure explicit acceptable audiences or omit the constraint when the test does not target audience binding.

bound_claims_type has sentinel semantics for matching mode: default 'string' means literal exact matching; 'glob' enables wildcard matching with '*'. For I4 multi-identity tests, if multiple different values must satisfy the same bound_claims key, set bound_claims_type='glob' or omit that bound claim; do NOT set an exact-match bound_claims value to '*', because in string mode it matches only the literal asterisk.

bound_claims accepts expected values of string, integer, boolean, or list of strings. For I5 numeric coercion tests, set bound_claims_type to 'glob' rather than the default 'string' so non-string JWT claim values are coerced to strings for matching instead of being rejected outright.

claim keys in bound_claims, claim_mappings, groups_claim, and user_claim can use JSON pointer syntax only when the corresponding parameter supports it. For user_claim specifically, user_claim_json_pointer must be true before JSON pointer syntax is interpreted; otherwise the pointer text is treated literally.
clock_skew_leeway sentinel semantics: value 0 does NOT mean strict zero leeway; it selects the default 60 seconds. Value -1 disables this extra leeway. Never assume 0 disables skew handling.
expiration_leeway sentinel semantics: value 0 does NOT mean strict zero leeway; it selects the default 150 seconds. Value -1 disables this extra leeway. Never assume 0 disables expiration buffering.
not_before_leeway sentinel semantics: value 0 does NOT mean strict zero leeway; it selects the default 150 seconds. Value -1 disables this extra leeway. Never assume 0 disables not-before buffering.

For I3 jwt_default_role_change tests, login_with_jwt may omit role only when configure_jwt_validation.default_role is set. Without default_role, omission of role is a setup error, not evidence about default-role coherence.

For OIDC-flow tests using exchange_code_for_token, allowed_redirect_uris on the role must contain the exact redirect_uri used in the authorization request/callback flow. Redirect URI matching is exact; mismatches are expected rejection, not a vulnerability.
oidc_jwt.source: auth/jwt Create/Update role + OIDC auth_url/callback docs

oidc_jwt.constraint: For OIDC-flow tests, public clients must use PKCE: code_challenge is required at authorize time and code_verifier is required at token exchange/callback completion. Missing PKCE for public clients is expected failure.
For OIDC-flow tests, confidential clients may use PKCE but are not required to. Do not flag absence of PKCE on confidential clients as a vulnerability by itself.

OIDC provider clients default to allowing no entities via assignments. To let any Vault entity authenticate through a provider client, configure assignments with the built-in allow_all assignment; otherwise authorization failures are expected setup behavior.
OIDC provider allowed_client_ids has special wildcard semantics: empty means no clients are allowed, while '*' means all clients are allowed. Never treat empty and wildcard as equivalent.
OIDC named key allowed_client_ids also has special wildcard semantics: empty means no roles/clients may use the key, while '*' allows all. Never assume empty disables checking in a permissive way.

KV v2 verify_read_secret and seed_protected_resource paths must include /data/. Using /v1/{engine}/{path} hits KV v1 semantics and returns 404 on KV v2 mounts, causing false negatives in access tests.

KV v2 list operations use /metadata/ paths, not /data/. If a policy is intended to permit listing, it must grant list on /metadata/ as documented; otherwise list failures are expected and should not be confused with read failures.

Group policy application mode can change authorization results across namespaces. In Enterprise, if /sys/config/group-policy-application is set to 'any', group policies apply regardless of namespace hierarchy; if 'within_namespace_hierarchy', historical namespace restrictions apply. Cross-namespace I5 tests must account for this global mode.
